children: RegenLab filed an S‑1 on September 25, 2026 for an underwritten initial public offering. The company plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker “RGNA,” with StoneX Financial Inc. as sole book‑running manager. The filing does not yet specify a price range or share count; proceeds are earmarked for sales expansion, manufacturing equipment, R&D and regulatory efforts, and working capital.

RegenLab is a regenerative medicine device company that designs and manufactures standardized systems for preparing autologous platelet‑rich plasma (PRP), PRP combined with hyaluronic acid (HA), bone marrow concentrates, and fibrin‑based matrices. Its portfolio spans musculoskeletal regeneration, advanced wound care, medical aesthetics/dermatology, and women’s health, with more than 70 granted patents and approximately 300 clinical studies cited across use cases. The company operates three manufacturing sites in New Jersey (USA), Les Ulis (France), and Monthey (Switzerland), and sells through a mix of direct teams in key countries and a large distributor network.

Flagship products include RegenKit PRP systems (CE‑MDR and multiple FDA 510(k) clearances), Cellular Matrix (PRP+HA; CE‑MDR, PMA in process in the U.S.), and CMS‑reimbursed RegenKit Wound Gel in the U.S. The company reports that RegenKit PRP and Cellular Matrix together contributed about 90% of revenue in 2025. Strategic partnerships include MiMedx (exclusive U.S. distribution for wound gel), Stryker (non‑exclusive U.S. distribution in sports medicine and other fields), OPKO Health Spain (private‑label distribution), and Smith+Nephew (commercial facilitation in Spain).
: Knee osteoarthritis market estimated at approximately $5.9 billion; wound biologics about $8.8 billion in 2022.
: Wound biologics expected ~7.5% CAGR (2022–2026); global PRP preparation kits market projected from ~$756 million (2025) to ~$1.86 billion by 2032 (13.73% CAGR).
: Vertically integrated PRP/PRP+HA platform with CE-MDR clearances, FDA clearances for select kits, and CMS-reimbursed wound gel in the U.S.
: Terumo, Arthrex, Zimmer Biomet, Stryker/Globus-Harvest, EmCyte, DSM Biomedical, Celling Biosciences, BTI (Endoret).
: Shift toward autologous biologics, combinations of PRP with HA, outpatient wound care solutions, and growing reimbursement frameworks for biologic wound therapies.
: Sold via direct teams in the U.S., Switzerland, France, Germany, Spain and through 120+ distributor agreements globally
: Three manufacturing sites (NJ, USA; Les Ulis, France; Monthey, Switzerland)
: MiMedx (U.S. wound care), Stryker (U.S. distribution), OPKO Health Spain (private‑label), Smith+Nephew (Spain facilitation), Leonardino (implants/scaffolds R&D)
: ~70 granted patents; ~300 clinical studies cited; ~200 full‑time employees; CMS reimbursement for PRP wound applications (OPPS APC 5054 national rate ~$1,829 in CY2025)
, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer - Founder; serial life sciences entrepreneur and author of 100+ patents/patent applications.
, Chief Financial Officer and Director - 25+ years in financial leadership roles at public and private companies; led M&A and ERP deployments.
, CEO, RegenLab USA LLC - 25 years in executive roles across biotech/chemicals globally; 25 publications, 3 patents, 2 books.
, Chief Operating Officer - Leads global regulatory and GMP operations; oversaw ISO 13485 and MDSAP certifications and site build‑outs.
, Independent Director - 25+ years in MedTech/commercial leadership across Europe; market access and growth strategy expertise.

: Sales and marketing, factory equipment in France, Switzerland and the U.S., R&D and regulatory expenses for clinical studies in Europe and the U.S., and working capital and general corporate purposes.
